stories.title: Australia’s security pact with Solomon Islands a blow to China’s influence in the Pacific
summary: Anthony Albanese and Matthew Wale sign new treaty as Solomon Islands PM states his country no longer ‘a source of uncertainty and doubt in the region’The Solomon Islands prime minister says the days of his country being an uncertain partner in the Pacific are over as he signed a sweeping agreement to make Australia the primary security partner and limit ties with China.Matthew Wale signed the new treaty with Australia’s prime minister, Anthony Albanese, in Canberra on Wednesday after Solomon Islands earlier this week announced it was terminating a landmark security pact with Beijing.

stories.title: Inflation rate jumps to 4.9% as Australia’s cost-of-living crisis intensifies
summary: Figure up from 4.3% annual rate in September and nearly double Reserve Bank’s official target of 2.5%Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updatesGet our daily political email, free app or daily news podcastSurging fuel costs and the end of electricity rebates have helped drive inflation to 4.9% in the year to October, from 4.3%, as cost-of-living pressures peak in the lead-up to Christmas.Alongside a 6.3% increase in fuel costs last month, the latest figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics showed electricity prices were 25% higher than a year earlier.

stories.title: Middle-aged women in England least likely to successfully quit smoking, study finds
summary: Of nearly 8,000 women who tried to stop, only 18% of those aged 45 to 60 managed to give upMiddle-aged women in England are the least likely to successfully give up smoking, according to research.Smoking is the leading cause of preventable death and illness in the UK.
While overall smoking rates in England have declined in recent decades, rates in some regions have increased.
About 6.75 million people smoke in England, of whom around 14% are women aged 45-60.

stories.title: US army to detonate 68 barrels of toxic lead in Iowa on day before Thanksgiving
summary: Residents warned to stay indoors amid conflicting information about how far the dust plume could travelThe US Army is set to detonate 68 barrels – five tons – of lead azide at an ammunition plant in rural Iowa on Wednesday morning, after delays and conflicting information about how far the toxic lead dust plume could travel after the explosion.That controlled blast has been scheduled for 10am ET on Wednesday, the day before the Thanksgiving holiday.

stories.title: Latest review of Met police culture finds little has changed since last one
summary: Failure to implement previous reports means institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia still present in forceMetropolitan police still institutionally racist and misogynist, says reportFrom the Stephen Lawrence inquiry in 1999 to Louise Casey’s landmark review in 2023, successive reports on the Metropolitan police have arrived at the same damning conclusion: Britain’s largest police force is institutionally racist.It will, therefore, come as little surprise that three years after Casey’s report, an independent review led by Gillian Fairfield has found that institutional racism, misogyny and homophobia persist within the force.

stories.title: UK to launch world’s first licensing scheme for knife sales
summary: Exclusive: Measures aimed at tackling grey market sellers known to sell dangerous knives to childrenMinisters will introduce the world’s first licensing scheme for businesses and private individuals selling all types of knives including cutlery, the Home Office announced on Wednesday.In a drive to fulfil the government’s pledge to halve knife crime within 10 years, shops and online vendors selling butter knives or machetes will be expected to apply for a licence or face fines.

stories.title: Metropolitan police still institutionally racist and misogynist, says report
summary: Independent review finds force has ‘fundamental systemic issues’ three years after damning report on Sarah Everard murderLatest review of Met police culture finds little has changed since last oneThe Metropolitan police remain institutionally racist, misogynistic and homophobic three years after a damning review into the force’s culture, a report has found.The investigation by Gillian Fairfield found “fundamental, systemic issues” and “institutional defensiveness” still existed in Britain’s biggest police force, which has struggled “to acknowledge racism as a structural problem”.

stories.title: England has largest frailty gap out of 31 countries, study finds
summary: People from lowest socioeconomic group in all countries studied had higher frailty scores than those in highest socioeconomic groupEngland has the largest gap between higher and lower socioeconomic groups when it comes to frailty compared with 30 other countries, a major study has found.The research, led by academics at King’s College London and published in BMC Medicine, looked at levels of frailty in 71,703 people from 31 countries including England, the US, China, France, Italy, the Netherlands, Sweden, Greece, Cyprus, Latvia and Lithuania.
